 Two Serie A clubs make enquiries about signing Federico Chiesa in January 2027
 Federico Chiesa has struggled to secure regular minutes at Liverpool this season.
 by Joseph Agbobli 30.10.2026 Add to Preferred Sources Follow DaveOCKOP: Add us as a preferred source on Google.
 Liverpool have strengthened their attacking options following Mohamed Salah’s departure, moving decisively to sign Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz.
 With Alexander Isak rediscovering his form and Hugo Ekitike working towards a return from injury, Andoni Iraola has plenty of options in attack.
 Rio Ngumoha, Cody Gakpo and Lewis Koumas also provide further depth, leaving uncertainty over the futures of some players already at the club, particularly Federico Chiesa.
 The 29-year-old joined Liverpool from Juventus in 2024 for £12.5million. However, despite being part of a Premier League title-winning squad, his time at Anfield has been frustrating.
 Injuries and periods of unavailability have restricted his involvement, while he has struggled to make a consistent impact when given opportunities.
 Inter Milan were linked with a move last summer transfer window, but a potential deal depended on Luis Henrique leaving the Italian club. That move failed to materialise, and Chiesa remained at Liverpool.
 According to Tuttomercatoweb, AC Milan and Lazio have made enquiries about the forward. Although Chiesa has been keen to remain in England and establish himself in the Premier League, Liverpool could now help change his stance.
 The club are expected to discuss his future with him, including the possibility of a January departure. Italian sides could favour an initial loan deal with an option to buy.
 Inter continue to monitor the situation, and a move could become more realistic if Luis Henrique leaves in January . Chiesa’s Liverpool contract runs until June 2028, but his wages could prove a stumbling block for potential suitors.
 His future beyond next summer remains uncertain, when he will enter the final year of his deal. Liverpool’s valuation of the former Juventus forward remains unknown.
 However, Italian clubs would favour an initial loan with an option to buy. Such an arrangement would limit the buyer’s risk over his fitness while allowing Liverpool to move him on without a permanent transfer fee dispute.
 Regardless of where he ends up, a return to Italy appears increasingly possible, with a January departure not out of the question.
